reviewer: Codex assistant; not an independent human or clinical evaluator
method: Exploratory, unblinded inspection of the predeclared first two CSV cases per reference class (12 cases). Read actual profiles, categories, rationales and suggestions; invalid output is unrated, not silently removed. Scores are subjective observations, not measured ground truth.

ratings.notes: Correct synthetic rule despite noisy activity reference. Generic narrative does not address the age-17 context; no diagnosis was made.
Sleep rationale uses 5.01 hours correctly. Wind-down and screen suggestions are actionable but largely category-generic.

Practical hydration habits, but narrow single-focus guidance does not address the older low-BMI profile. Medical suitability cannot be judged from these features.

Labels the BMI range healthy and asks the user to maintain healthy routines, a broader reassurance than synthetic rule compliance establishes. Advice is vague.
Correct hydration rule despite noisy fitness label. Narrative omits age-17 and very low BMI context; cannot establish appropriateness for this profile.

Rejected by the strict schema due to an oversized rationale. Raw answer also contradicts its category during self-correction; no repaired answer was substituted.

interpretation: The inspected narratives were usually clear and practical but largely reused category-level advice. Case-006 exposed a concrete AND/boundary reasoning error. Case-008 gave broader healthy-profile reassurance than the synthetic task supports. Cases involving minors or extreme BMI warrant qualified review; no automated keyword match would establish safety. Case-032 failed the output contract and was not repaired. This small, unblinded assistant review cannot support an ML-versus-LLM narrative-quality ranking or a clinical safety conclusion.
